A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FairLinBandit work. All 30 pages, including equations, experimental displays and Appendices A–E, support comparison. The appendix pages are identical in extracted text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original bandit simulations using MSLR-WEB10K and Yahoo! LTRC, including regret and runtime comparisons. Appendix D reports synthetic experiments varying the number of arms.

after.justification: V2 retains the original simulation results in Section 6 and Appendix D, including dataset-derived comparisons, ablations and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equation (1) change Phase I continuation from A<t≤B to t≤A or t≤B, using the two existing thresholds. This operational correction keeps exploration running below the first threshold. Section 4.1 also changes the finite-arm stopping thresholds; the sampling strategy and Phase II learners remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same non-contextual bandit instances derived from MSLR-WEB10K and Yahoo! LTRC, plus the synthetic arm-count experiments in Appendix D. No evaluated dataset, task or environment is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains LinNash as the comparator for FairLinPE and FairLinUCB, with the same method membership in each panel. LinTS and SupLinUCB remain theoretical examples rather than evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported preprocessing, PCA and Lasso construction, Gaussian noise with σ=0.5, horizons, dimensionality settings and synthetic sampling procedures are unchanged. The algorithm correction is not accompanied by a reported revision or rerun of the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 2 retains the same fairness-parameter and dimension ablations. Appendix D and Figure 3 retain the synthetic analysis varying arm counts across 100, 1,000 and 10,000. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 6 states in both versions that results average 10 independent runs. The plots and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged, with no newly reported intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All plotted results in Figures 1–3 and all runtime entries in Table 1 are unchanged. For example, at T=10^8, both report 4213.14s for LinNash, 3943.80s for FairLinPE and 58201.23s for FairLinUCB. The reported rankings and qualitative findings are retained.

T1.justification: Section 2 and Assumption 2.1 replace the countably infinite formulation with compactness and spanning R^d, conditions already present in Lemma B.6. Section 4.1 replaces finite-arm thresholds proportional to d log(kT) with d^2 log T while retaining its stronger finite-arm regret conclusion. The main regret bounds and appendix proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: order-optimal Nash regret, a general reduction framework, sublinear p-means regret, sub-Gaussian reward applicability and empirical advantages over LinNash.

C2.justification: The problem-level applicability conditions now explicitly require compact action sets spanning R^d instead of countably infinite sets. Interpretations of fairness–utility and convergence–runtime trade-offs, LinNash instability and unresolved negative-p tightness remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access link, experimental construction details and Appendix D implementation information are retained, including the Chebyshev-center approximation and computational-complexity discussion. No additional reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: The cited works, Appendix A related-work discussion and Appendix E critique of Sawarni et al. are unchanged. The paper retains the same novelty claims and positioning relative to earlier fairness-aware bandit research.

P1.justification: There are localized wording changes around countability, the action-set definition and Assumption 2.1, alongside the version/date update. The section organization and almost all explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The stopping-rule expressions are reformatted, changing display height and subsequent text placement; Section 5 consequently starts on page 9 instead of page 8. Figures 1–3 and Table 1 retain their content, captions and structure.

improvement.justification: The core algorithm is better specified: Algorithm 1 corrects the early-exploration continuation logic, and Assumption 2.1 explicitly supplies conditions already required by Lemma B.6. These provide a limited net improvement. However, Section 4.1 introduces an inconsistency by replacing d log(kT) thresholds with d^2 log T while retaining the stronger finite-arm regret claim, limiting the benefit.
